claims.exact_statement: Sereda et al. report that age-related CMA decline alters senescent-cell secretomes, suppresses macrophage CMA/phagocytosis/survival, and is associated with persistent senescence and slower wound repair; systemic CA77.1 lowers several senescence markers in aged mice and disease readouts in a bleomycin model.
claims.scope: Published cell, mouse and human-lung observations under the paper's specific protocols; no independent replication in this task.
claims.measurement_boundary: KFERQ-Dendra reports CMA cargo delivery; SA-β-gal, p21, HMGB1 and gene scores are proxies; bead fluorescence is bead uptake; wound size and fibrosis are tissue-level endpoints. No joint in-vivo clearance/birth-rate observation was made here.
claims.novelty_boundary: Biological mechanism is published. No new aging mechanism, clinical outcome or priority claim is asserted.
claims.next_gate: Compartment-restricted manipulation with lineage-resolved senescent-target birth, macrophage survival and target uptake measured in the same tissue and animals.

claims.exact_statement: Descriptive extraction of Sereda et al. Fig. 4 source data gives Fig. 4h means of 14.6267 (control secretome/no CA), 2.6143 (CMA-deficient secretome/no CA), and 6.3909 (CMA-deficient secretome/CA); the CA mean closes 31.44% of the no-CA gap. Fig. 4e group means are 53.47% versus 2.94% efferocytosis for control versus CMA-deficient macrophages with untreated fibroblasts, and 45.13% versus 2.58% with senescent fibroblasts; the paper reports ANOVA variance shares 98.22% macrophage genotype, 0.8562% fibroblast state and 0.7214% interaction.
assumptions: Workbook labels and reported group assignments are correctly transcribed.
Fig. 4e has n=3 independent experiments; descriptive means are reported without a new inferential test.
Fig. 4h fields are nested within three independent experiments; fields are not treated as independent biological replicates.
claims.scope_limit: Fig. 4e measures efferocytosis of staurosporine-killed targets; Fig. 4h measures IgG-bead uptake. Neither is a living senescent-cell clearance rate or tissue-repair probability.
claims.novelty_boundary: A descriptive reanalysis of the source data; not a new mechanism, theory, independent replication, or causal intervention result.
claims.falsifier: A correctly parsed source workbook with group labels or values inconsistent with the extractor output.

claims.exact_statement: A proposal to bypass macrophage CMA decline by blocking CD47/SIRPα/QPCT-L is already covered in relevant part by Schloesser et al., who report that checkpoint-axis or QPCT/L interference reverses senescent-cell-mediated suppression of bystander efferocytosis; CD47 loss alone did not induce engulfment of senescent cells.
claims.scope_limit: This blocks a generic checkpoint-bypass novelty claim but does not show that every tissue or senescent-cell type is fully cleared.
claims.next_gate: Only reconsider with a distinct, measured macrophage survival or lineage-resolution mechanism not covered by this checkpoint work.

claims.exact_statement: Under an exchangeable genotype-blind N-copy Moran model, the probability that a neutral k-copy allele reaches m copies before loss is k/m; mutation-supply weighting yields a conditional source-parameter accounting identity, while turnover rescales finite-horizon event time and selection may reverse its effect.
assumptions: Fixed copy number, neutral equal replication/removal, no mutation after focal origin for the threshold result, no cell division or selection.
Mutation-supply calculation uses an infinite-sites neutral origin model and does not equate threshold crossing to cell dysfunction.
claims.novelty_boundary: Neutral drift variance, time-rescaling and exact finite-population threshold analysis are prior art. No new mitochondrial mechanism is claimed.

claims.exact_statement: In a stationary one-crypt source model, a candidate Paneth-production route obeys 0.15 D p c <= P/tau_P; pooled equal-crypt renewal fraction q and calibrated threshold tau bound the crypt coverage pi by max(0,(q-tau)/(1-tau)) <= pi <= min(1,q/tau). These are conditional accounting/identifiability statements, not biological estimates.
assumptions: Stationary mature Paneth-cell pool and replacement flux P/tau_P.
The source's approximately 0.15 asymmetric division fraction applies to the modeled +3/+4 ISC division flux D.
Equal crypt weighting and calibrated local threshold tau for the coverage inequality.
claims.novelty_boundary: Mass-balance and probability bounds are standard; focal organelle-age/αKG mechanism is published primary work. D, P, residence time, output c and functional threshold are not jointly measured.

claims.exact_statement: Recent CMA and glutamine-flux MuSC studies report aged-cell interventions and acute transplantation/regeneration readouts, but the inspected primary evidence does not provide repeated-injury reserve trajectories or joint single-cell lineage/fate rates needed to validate a reserve-preserving intervention model.
claims.novelty_boundary: A generic stem-pool branching model or metabolic flux allocation restatement is not claimed as new.

claims.exact_statement: This branch establishes no new quantitative aging-control capability, causal cell-clearance law, validated regeneration intervention, or human clinical result.
